[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is possible to design a system without the momentary pause.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] One approach is to use a flow-based pressure sensing mechanism that can measure tire pressure while air is flowing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The method involves creating a pressure drop across an orifice or flow restrictor, which allows the pressure sensor to measure the tire pressure accurately.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 1: Install a flow restrictor or an orifice in the air passage between the compressor and the tire.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The flow restrictor creates a pressure drop across itself when air flows through it, isolating the tire pressure from the air hose and compressor pressure.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 2: Use a pressure sensor that measures the pressure on the tire side of the flow restrictor or orifice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The sensor could be a mechanical (e.g., Bourdon tube, diaphragm) or electronic sensor (e.g., piezoelectric, strain gauge).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 3: Allow the user to set the desired tire pressure using a dial or a digital interface.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 4: Connect the pressure sensor to a pressure-sensitive valve or a solenoid valve.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The valve would remain closed during the tire inflation process.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 5: When the tire pressure reaches the desired value, the pressure sensor sends a signal to the pressure-sensitive valve or solenoid valve, causing it to open.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This will release excess air from the system, preventing further inflation of the tire.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 6: The valve would close once the pressure inside the tire drops slightly below the desired pressure, stopping the release of air.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This ensures that the tire remains at the desired pressure after the excess air is released.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A flow-based pressure sensing mechanism allows for continuous inflation while ensuring the pressure relief mechanism activates at the correct pressure level.  
[USER] How could you make step 5 mechanical rather than electronic?  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To create a mechanical pressure-sensitive valve activation mechanism, you can use a mechanical pressure switch or a spring-loaded valve.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 1: Replace the electronic pressure sensor and solenoid valve with a mechanical pressure switch or spring-loaded valve.
